sources.entry: 1time - Zero-knowledge one-time secret sharing. Create a one-time link for a password, API key, or file. Encrypted client-side in the browser, never reaches the server in plaintext, self-destructs after the allowed number of views (one by default). (Demo, Source Code) MIT Docker

summary.one_liner: A self-hostable zero-knowledge tool for sharing passwords, API keys, text, and encrypted files through one-time, self-destructing links.
summary.what_it_does: Secrets are encrypted in the browser with AES-256-GCM (keys derived via HKDF-SHA256) before upload, so the server stores only encrypted data. The encryption key sits in the URL fragment, which is never sent to the server. The sender uploads only a SHA-256 hash of the read token, and the server deletes the stored blob after the last allowed view. Text secrets can allow a few views, while file links default to one download and can allow up to 10. The project includes built-in password, passphrase, API key, and WiFi password generators, plus a first-party CLI (@1time/cli) for piping secrets from a terminal. A browser extension is also provided. The backend is Go with Redis, and the frontend is a static Astro build served by nginx, deployable with Docker Compose.
use_cases: share a password with a colleague via one-time link
send an API key without leaving it in chat logs
transfer an encrypted file with a one-download link
pipe secrets from a terminal in DevOps scripts
generate passwords, passphrases, or WiFi passwords
how_to_run: curl -O (download docker-compose file from README link)
Edit .env: set APP_HOSTNAME to your domain
notable: Zero-knowledge design: the key stays in the URL fragment and the server stores only a hash of the read token
Encrypted file sharing with one-time download links
First-party CLI with send/read and send-file/read-file commands
Built-in password, passphrase, API key, and WiFi password generators
caveats: Hosted instance and self-hosting both require a separate reverse proxy for HTTPS/TLS termination, which the operator must set up
Redis is required as a dependency, and a VM deployment path needs nginx and Redis installed by the script
README lists no explicit limits beyond pointing to a developer page for limits
keywords: send a password to someone safely
